_comment: Largs Community Council issue register. Each entry is an ISSUE, not a monthly note: `id` is permanent and never reused, so when later minutes are digested the item is UPDATED in place rather than added again, and its earlier appearances are listed in `alsoRecorded`. STATUS DESCRIBES THE RECORD, NOT THE WORLD — it says what the minutes record at the last mention, never what may have happened since. raised = recorded, no action yet assigned or taken. progress = an action is assigned and the minutes record it moving. completed = the minutes record it done. no-update = the item appears in two or more meetings with nothing new recorded. Nothing is rated, ranked or scored, and no status implies criticism of anyone. Every entry is read against the source minutes before it is pushed.
_rules: A SCHEDULE IS NOT A COMPLETION. 'Will take place on 25/02/25' is a plan; unless a later meeting records it happening, the status is not completed.

A QUALIFICATION TRAVELS WITH ITS COMPLETION. Where the minutes record a caveat alongside a result — no oversight of a fund, a decision LCC disagreed with — the caveat is part of the entry, not an omission.
COMPLETED MEANS DETERMINED, NOT SATISFACTORY. Waterside Street is completed because the council reached a determination, not because anyone was pleased with it. The status key on the page says so.

DECISIONS ARE NAMED, LOSING MOTIONS ARE NOT. Proposers and seconders of carried motions appear as the minutes give them. Where a motion was not supported, the decision is recorded without naming who proposed the alternative.
NO PLANNING APPLICATIONS. Per the decision of 4 August 2026, individual applications are out of scope site-wide. Applications discussed in the 2025 minutes are deliberately absent from this register.

MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC ARE NOT NAMED, and neither is the substance of their personal circumstances, even where the minutes describe them. People acting in a public capacity — councillors, MSPs, officers, named volunteers thanked in the record — are named as the minutes give them.
SOURCE TYPOS ARE PRESERVED rather than silently corrected, except that official spellings of real people's names beat minute typos.
WHERE A FIGURE IS ILLEGIBLE IN THE SOURCE IT IS OMITTED, not guessed. The Memory Walk total is printed as '£100 0' in the July minutes and is therefore not stated here.

POLICE REPORTS ARE NOT DIGESTED. Where the police have asked for a matter to be communicated to the public, and it concerns something residents can act on, it may be recorded as a public-safety notice — never with individuals, premises, figures or ongoing investigations.

OFFICERS ARE NAMED BY ROLE, NOT BY NAME. Elected members, MSPs and senior officers appearing in a public capacity are named as the minutes give them. Council officers below that level are identified by role: they did not stand for anything, and the register should not make one person the face of an institutional delay.
A MINUTE'S ADJECTIVES NEVER TRAVEL. The minutes contain words like 'farce', 'appalling', 'amazing' and 'lively'. None belongs in a register that rates nothing.
NOTHING IS RECORDED ABOUT A DEATH, an ongoing fatal accident enquiry, or a memorial arising from one. In a town this size the family is identifiable to every local reader.

coverage.note: Built from the approved minutes of sixteen meetings — nine in 2025 (January, February, April, May, June, July, August, September and November) and six in 2026 (January to June) — together with December 2024 where an item began there. Minutes for March, October and December 2025 are not in the published archive; the October and December meetings are both recorded as having taken place, their minutes having been approved at the meetings that followed. Where an item's last mention is some time ago, that describes the written record and nothing more.

statuses.label: All items
statuses.blurb: Every item in the register, newest record first.

statuses.label: Completed
statuses.blurb: Items the minutes record as done. Completed describes the record — that a matter was determined, not that everyone was satisfied with the outcome.

statuses.label: In progress
statuses.blurb: An action is assigned and the minutes record it moving.

statuses.label: Raised
statuses.blurb: Recorded in the minutes, with no action yet assigned or taken.

statuses.label: No recent update
statuses.blurb: The item appears in two or more meetings with nothing new recorded. No criticism is implied — minutes are a record of what was said, not of everything that happened.

digest.title: Christmas food support
digest.summary: £2,000 was ringfenced for Christmas food support — dinners at Largs Naz Church and BEC, Common Ground meals, the Foodbank and the Food Hub.
digest.responsible: LCC Access to Food group. Proposed by CCllr Stevenson, agreed by all.

digest.title: A banking hub for the town
digest.summary: Information drop-in sessions for the Largs Cash Hub were arranged at the Bank of Scotland on 16 June and 21 July 2026, 10am to 2pm.
digest.responsible: Cash Access UK, with Kenneth Gibson MSP.

digest.title: Community Council membership
digest.summary: Kerry Canning was appointed to the Community Council, and Alexander Hughes appointed adviser for youth.
digest.nextStep: A new youth group — Alex with Tom, Robbie, Jamie and Kerry — to agree a plan.

digest.title: The Chair is to step down in early 2026
digest.summary: CCllr Stewart took over as interim Chair in January 2026, and tribute was paid to the outgoing Chair. By June 2026 CCllr Woodburn was chairing meetings.

digest.title: Mackerston play area
digest.summary: Around £350,000 of play-park funding is expected, and the Community Council has asked North Ayrshire Council for the plans.
digest.responsible: LCC to NAC, following Kenneth Gibson MSP's enquiry.

digest.title: Handrail for the beach steps at May Street
digest.summary: A handrail for the beach steps is still being pursued with North Ayrshire Council, after two reported injuries.
digest.responsible: Cllr Murdoch with NAC. LCC following progress.

digest.title: School crossing patrol at Glenacre Avenue
digest.summary: The possible loss of a school crossing patrol was raised at the February 2025 meeting as one of the budget proposals, to be decided at the Council's budget meeting later that month. That budget, on 26 February 2025, approved removing the patrol at the junction of Glenacre Avenue and Alexander Avenue, beside the primary school. A Freedom of Information request by CCllr Woodburn found the assessment had been carried out between 4pm and 4.30pm, well after the school comes out, and referred to markings for a mini roundabout that does not exist there. LCC challenged the assessment as invalid and wrote to the Head of Service and the five elected members. In May the Council acknowledged the flawed assessment and reversed the decision. The minutes record that reversal for other areas which lost their patrols was not supported.
digest.responsible: North Ayrshire Council, following a challenge led by CCllr Woodburn.

digest.title: A community minibus for Largs
digest.summary: The application for a community minibus was successful and the full amount of the grant was awarded. Largs Thistle is the owner and keeper of the vehicle.
digest.responsible: North Ayrshire Council Locality Partnership. Application pursued by LCC.

digest.title: ScotRail on the Largs line
digest.summary: A protest at Largs station was announced for the morning after the January meeting, over cuts to the hours of ticket office staff, and concern was recorded about the impact on the public. ScotRail's Strategy and Planning Director, Scott Prentice, attended the February meeting and answered questions on journey times, carriage numbers and staffing on evening trains. On the ticket office he said the change was to the office's opening hours rather than to staff hours, with the same number of staff and their duties altered to spend more time on the platform.

digest.title: Memory Walk
digest.summary: The Memory Walk has taken place each year since 2023. The 2025 walk was held on 22 June at Barrfields Stadium for Dementia Friendly Largs, and the 2026 walk at Barrfields on 21 June, open to all. An application to the Common Good Fund towards it was successful.
digest.responsible: LCC, with KA Leisure and Dementia Friendly Largs.

digest.title: Community garden seasonal displays
digest.summary: The community garden carried seasonal displays through 2025 and into 2026 — Easter, VE Day, a summer display, VJ Day in August, the Viking Festival, Hallowe'en, Remembrance and Christmas, then a World Cup theme in 2026. CCllr Adair and residents of Sandringham took over the flower beds, and a local resident donated large plants. Thanks were recorded at the 2025 AGM to Fiona Stevenson for the artwork and to the members who work in the garden. The garden costs about £150 to £200 a year and LCC is considering ways to raise it.

digest.title: Love Largs litter signs at the school
digest.summary: Love Largs emoji litter signs were displayed at the school and around the town through 2025, and continued to go up during 2026 — at Bake n Bite in February and Fishworks by June. Separately, in February 2025 the Academy's newsletter highlighted pupils dropping litter, and LCC agreed to supply additional posters for display throughout the school at a cost of about £90. One spare sign remained.
digest.responsible: LCC litter campaign, with local businesses, Largs Academy and the Youth Forum.

digest.title: Stakis Foundation funding for Access to Food
digest.summary: Access to Food work through the year was supported by funding from the Stakis Foundation, which enabled LCC to support Christmas dinners at Largs Naz Church, the weekly Common Ground meals, and Christmas dinners at BEC for the Team Challenge group. The Foodbank and Largs Food Hub were also supported.

digest.title: Community cinema showings
digest.summary: Community cinema showings ran during the year. The charge changed to a flat fee of £100 a showing regardless of screen size. Suggestions for films were invited, and a buffet alongside a showing was raised as something that might be trialled. LCC agreed to apply to the Participatory Budget to host a movie night for families, including those with additional support needs, with food, in January or February. A school cinema event at Barrfields was recorded in November as unlikely to go ahead this year.

digest.title: Annual accounts audited
digest.summary: The accounts for the year ending 31 August 2025 were audited by North Ayrshire Council and approved at the AGM. At the year end the Admin account stood at £1.05, the Project account at £3,990.17 and the Cinema account at £678.07.
digest.responsible: CCllr Wood as Treasurer, audited by North Ayrshire Council.

digest.title: Railfuture invited to a meeting
digest.summary: Railfuture was invited in August 2025 to discuss strategies for lobbying for improvements to the North Coast line, including faster and more frequent services and enhanced services in summer and for events such as the Viking Festival. Railfuture attended the February 2026 meeting and set out its aims for rail passengers. The advice recorded was to form a rail user group, engage with ScotRail's Strategy and Planning Director, and raise the service as a campaigning issue. Two actions followed: to identify the successor to the previous ScotRail director, and to request the cancellation rate for Largs under freedom of information.

digest.title: Closure of Farmfoods
digest.summary: Following the closure of Farmfoods, a licensing application was received in March 2026 for a proposed grocery store in the former premises, to which the Community Council recorded no objection. The loading bay outside is to remain, no order having been received to remove the loading restriction.

digest.title: Opening hours at Largs Campus
digest.summary: LCC continued to press for longer public opening at the Largs Campus. KA Leisure advised in March 2026 that it was still trying to extend times but could not do so because of operating leases. The Community Council agreed to invite KA Leisure's Chief Executive to a meeting. In June it was recorded that a karate club had to take forty children to Garnock Academy for a grading because Largs Academy could not be opened.
digest.responsible: KA Leisure. Pursued by LCC and Cllr Murdoch.

digest.title: Places for young people to meet
digest.summary: A member of the public asked in August 2025 what was being done for young people, noting a lack of awareness of what already exists; an open football pitch and IT upskilling were suggested, and the young person was invited to work with LCC. In November Alexander Hughes was appointed an Appointed Adviser on youth in the community, having raised the lack of places for young people to meet and get support and an interest in mental health among them, and a group was set up to agree a plan. Space was secured at Vikingar for a Youth Project Safe Space, with an introductory event in February 2026 and £160 agreed towards advertising. In April a taster musical workshop was hosted free of charge at Largs Naz Church as part of a youth mental health initiative, leading to a six-week block being planned, with further events discussed at Largs Academy.
digest.responsible: LCC youth group, with Vikingar, KA Leisure and Largs Academy.

digest.title: Cairneys Quay renovation
digest.summary: Cairneys Quay Association reported renovation work on the quay, slipway and toilets, and the need to raise £150,000 for its future. Ideas for fundraising were invited.

digest.title: Community Council elections
digest.summary: Community Council elections were postponed from 2025: the Chair recommended waiting because of the timescales of the Scheme of Establishment review, and a motion to hold them in 2025 was not supported. They were then expected in September or October 2026. In June 2026, with the review still incomplete, it was agreed by all to postpone again until it concludes — proposed by CCllr Phillips, seconded by CCllr Stevenson.
digest.responsible: Largs Community Council, pending North Ayrshire Council's review.

digest.title: Road safety at Waterside Street
digest.summary: Concern was raised in July 2025 about sight lines when leaving driveways on Waterside Street because of parked cars, and separately about traffic at the bottom of Waterside Street and Main Street and the state of the pavements. Both were referred to the elected councillors as the route to take them forward. In September North Ayrshire Council advised that none of its criteria were met for any work on Waterside Street.

digest.title: Licensing of shops selling vapes
digest.summary: In response to concern about the number of shops selling vapes, it was reported that licensing will not be introduced in Scotland, because vape shops are regulated through a mandatory retailer register.

digest.title: Access to Food terms of reference
digest.summary: The Access to Food group met on 9 September and agreed updated terms of reference to reflect changes in Community Council membership.

digest.title: Public toilets, including Aubery
digest.summary: In February 2025 it was recorded that public toilets would remain open all summer, that Aubery would be reinstated in some way and that Mackerston would close. In May concerns were raised about the cost of repairs at Aubery and the lack of documentation from North Ayrshire Council, with a suggestion to use the working toilet as a multi-sex facility meantime. In July LCC proposed that part of a repurposed £1.25m be used to reopen Aubery. In August the Viking Festival provided portaloos during the festival, LCC recorded that it would like more say in how the seafront car park fund is spent, and Kenneth Gibson MSP agreed to take the question forward. In September the Council set out the cost of refurbishment, the position on Aubery and the funds available from the car park, and recorded its view that Largs is well provided for at Gallowgate, Broomfields and the Pencil.
digest.responsible: North Ayrshire Council. Pursued by LCC and Kenneth Gibson MSP.

digest.title: Gondola proposal from the Local Place Plan
digest.summary: A proposal for an aerial gondola, arising from the Largs Local Place Plan, was approached tentatively by a company in February 2025 and a letter of intent was signed with Gondola Ventures in April. The company visited Largs in May for a feasibility study hosted by LCC, with North Coast councillors invited; CCllr Alexander emphasised that the project was at a very early stage. A Zoom meeting followed in July, and in August a meeting took place with the company and landowners, recorded as being under non-disclosure. By September it was described as an ongoing, long-term project.
digest.responsible: Gondola Ventures with LCC. Point of contact CCllr Alexander.

digest.title: Sound loop in the Valhalladrome
digest.summary: The absence of a sound loop in the Valhalladrome at Vikingar was raised, with the Hakkison Lecture given as an occasion where many people struggle to hear. LCC agreed to raise it with the management.

digest.title: Support for the Brisbane Observatory Trust
digest.summary: An invitation to the Observatory Trust to speak to the Community Council was agreed in April 2025. After its presentation in June, LCC agreed to host a meeting of community groups later in the year in support of restoring the Observatory, for which £158,000 is required; LCC recorded that it was keen to help particularly because of the Olympic Games being held in Brisbane in 2032. The Trust has obtained a lease on the building, which is now listed. Kenneth Gibson MSP offered support with any future plans. The action was carried forward at each meeting to September.

digest.title: Invitation to senior police officers
digest.summary: It was agreed in 2025 to invite senior officers to a meeting. The Ayrshire Police Divisional Commander attended in March 2026 and set out local policing priorities, the review of resourcing in North Ayrshire, and the establishment of community investigation hubs.
digest.responsible: Police Scotland. Invitation issued by LCC.

digest.title: Crossing warden at Holehouse Road
digest.summary: The absence of a school crossing warden at the junction of Holehouse Road and Alexander Avenue was raised. North Ayrshire Council replied explaining the staffing position and said it hoped to have someone in place soon.

digest.title: Linn Avenue play park
digest.summary: Play park equipment was ordered for installation over the summer. Concern was raised in June about ground levels at the new play area being unsafe for children, and a letter was sent to North Ayrshire Council. A time capsule was bought for an opening ceremony. In August the new park was compared with what has been provided in Irvine and Kilwinning. Kenneth Gibson MSP confirmed that it is for the local authority to decide how funding received from the Scottish Government is spent, that North Ayrshire should be allocated equitably, and that it falls to the five elected councillors to see that it is; he agreed to raise the strategy for play areas, and how much has been allocated, with North Ayrshire Council. Concern was recorded about the lack of response to freedom of information requests.
digest.responsible: North Ayrshire Council. Concerns pursued by CCllr Alexander and CCllr Woodburn.

digest.title: The Helter Skelter youth fund
digest.summary: An application form was constructed with the trustees and young people, and the online application process went live in April 2025, running to 30 April, with the trustees deciding on applications. Around £70,000 remained in July, with applications due to reopen in October. LCC recorded that it has no oversight of how the fund is disbursed. CCllr Alexander advised in February 2025 that the charity's accounts had not yet been submitted to the Scottish charity register for that year.

digest.title: Open letter on the i3 site money
digest.summary: LCC agreed to write an open letter to the five elected members proposing that £1.25m allocated to the i3 site in Irvine be repurposed and shared between communities, with Largs's share going towards a community minibus, flower beds on the promenade and, subject to funds remaining, works to reopen the Aubery toilets. Other community councils were to be asked to support the approach.
digest.responsible: CCllr Woodburn. Proposed by CCllr Woodburn, seconded by CCllr Low Thomson, agreed by all.

digest.title: Freedom of Information request on the i3 site
digest.summary: The Freedom of Information response about the disposal of the i3 site in Irvine was received, after the original response had passed its deadline.
digest.responsible: North Ayrshire Council. Request made by CCllr Woodburn.

digest.title: The Participatory Budget process
digest.summary: Questions were raised in January 2025 about the Participatory Budget: a voting system that appeared to favour larger groups, the same groups succeeding each year, no feedback given to unsuccessful applicants, and whether a biannual system would be fairer. It was the first year the budget had been oversubscribed. In February the Council advised the process was being evaluated, recommended that groups encourage people to vote for them, and undertook to note that unsuccessful groups are not told their vote numbers. No later minutes record the outcome of that evaluation. A drop-in session for interested groups was held at Largs Library in August 2025, £1,000 was paid to LCC in January 2026, and funding remained available in May 2026 towards boards at the community garden.

digest.title: Buying energy at a reduced rate for local businesses
digest.summary: The effect of high energy prices on local businesses was raised, together with an arrangement by which local communities can buy energy at a reduced rate. Businesses would need to be involved.
digest.responsible: CCllr Low Thomson was to investigate further.

digest.title: Blanket 20mph speed limit
digest.summary: North Ayrshire Council's Cabinet decided on a blanket 20mph limit across North Ayrshire, implemented through temporary traffic regulations, with all streets requiring new signage. CCllr Woodburn reported that the decision was taken without consultation, that a full debate of all councillors had been refused, and that the accident statistics did not support it. The view of those present in June 2025 was that a blanket limit was not required and should instead be targeted. In April 2026 Cllr Murdoch described it as a temporary arrangement with an eighteen-month consultation period. The cost is borne by the Scottish Government.
digest.responsible: North Ayrshire Council, under Scottish Government policy.

digest.title: Joining Railfuture
digest.summary: Largs Community Council agreed to join the rail campaigning group Railfuture at £25 a year, to press for better services on the Largs line. Proposed by CCllr Woodburn, seconded by CCllr Low Thomson.

digest.title: Freedom of Information request on council employees resident in England
digest.summary: North Ayrshire Council responded to a Freedom of Information request about the number of its employees resident in England, stating there are three. No further information was given, and further detail was being sought.
digest.responsible: North Ayrshire Council. Request made by a local newspaper reporter.

digest.title: Litter sign at Vikingar
digest.summary: The Love Largs litter sign at Vikingar, reported broken in April, was repaired.

digest.title: Free school lunches at Largs library
digest.summary: The Secretary raised that free school lunches were available in libraries across North Ayrshire except Largs, and recorded the expectation that this was a clerical error.

digest.title: Request for a trustee position on the Helter Skelter board
digest.summary: A letter from LCC to the Chair of Helter Skelter requesting a trustee position remained unanswered. The minutes record LCC's disappointment that its offer to be involved had not been responded to.
digest.responsible: Helter Skelter trustees. Pursued by CCllr Alexander and Cllr Hill.

digest.title: Condition of the Helter Skelter site
digest.summary: Scaffolding at the site was examined and made safe in February, following concern about the condition of the site, and rubbish at the rear was being cleared by April.
digest.responsible: North Ayrshire Council, following a request from Cllr Marshall.

digest.title: Hunterston representation
digest.summary: CCllr Macintosh took over as the Community Council's representative on Hunterston matters, nominated by CCllr Woodburn and seconded by the Chair. This resolved the gap in representation recorded in December 2024.

digest.title: The Largs Local Place Plan
digest.summary: North Ayrshire Council approved the registration of the Largs Local Place Plan. The plan was produced by members of the Community Council and adopted by it in December 2024 after consultation, on a motion proposed by CCllr Adair and seconded by CCllr Low Thomson.
digest.responsible: North Ayrshire Council. Plan produced by the LCC Local Place Plan group.

digest.title: Access to Food tea dance
digest.summary: A tea dance was held on 20 February at the Masonic Hall as a joint fundraiser with Dementia Friendly Largs, Largs Food Hub and the Access to Food group.

digest.title: Meeting with North Ayrshire Council on housing
digest.summary: A meeting with the Head of Housing to discuss housing issues in Largs was arranged for 25 February. The minutes record the arrangement but no account of the meeting.
digest.responsible: CCllr Woodburn with North Ayrshire Council.

digest.title: Closures at the recycling centre
digest.summary: Residents raised concern about repeated closures, most recently one of four days with no reason given. A Freedom of Information request was made about how often the centre had closed in the past year and the reasons. The most recent closure was attributed to staff attending a three-day first aid course, and the booking system was moving online. North Ayrshire Council offered to give a presentation on waste and recycling, and one was requested for the March meeting, though by February no response had been received about attending. Concern was expressed about a possible increase in fly tipping.
digest.responsible: North Ayrshire Council. Request made by CCllr Alexander.

digest.title: Rose garden section of the community garden
digest.summary: Approval was given to obtain a quotation for chippings and a weed barrier for the rose garden section, on a motion proposed by CCllr Low Thomson and seconded by CCllr Adair, and the upgrade was recorded as ongoing in February.

digest.title: Funding for Largs Food Hub
digest.summary: Funding for the Food Hub was due to end in October, which was not known when the hub opened. The two meetings name the funder differently — Scottish Government funding in January, North Ayrshire Council funding in February. Concern was recorded about its viability after only a year, and about how much is expected of volunteers. A larder network meeting in March was to discuss finances.
digest.responsible: The Locality Partnership was to consider the issue.

digest.title: Pavement parking rules
digest.summary: East Castle Avenue is the only street in Largs with a partial exemption from the pavement parking ban; other streets did not meet the Scottish Government's criteria on road and pavement width. Parking on a privately owned pavement is still liable to a fine. Concern was recorded about emergency vehicle access and about a general lack of communication. A letter to Transport Scotland and to the relevant Scottish Government committee was agreed in December, and clarification on road widths was sought from Kenneth Gibson MSP in January.
digest.responsible: Scottish Government legislation, administered by North Ayrshire Council.

digest.title: The date of Yuletide evening
digest.summary: Several businesses suggested moving Yuletide evening to a different day. The minutes record that most businesses had not asked the Events Committee to change it and that there was no consensus, and that the Events Committee would continue to consider the options.

digest.title: Roads and pavements, and AMEY's management of the A78
digest.summary: Residents raising the condition of pavements in June 2025 were advised to email AMEY Highways directly. In August residents were asked to send photographs of roads or pavements needing improvement to the Community Council's Facebook page or email address. The Community Council recorded dissatisfaction with several aspects of AMEY's management of the A78 and agreed to seek to engage with the company, either privately or at a public meeting. The matters listed were the Fort Road traffic junction, the M&S crossing being out of action, flooding at Geraldo's, road closures with unsuitable diversions, the resurfacing of the A78 and damaged manholes, and a lack of community engagement.
digest.responsible: AMEY. The Chair to take forward on behalf of LCC.

digest.title: Allotments at Douglas Park
digest.summary: A proposal for allotments at Douglas Park was raised by a member of the public, who has drawn up a plan he would like considered. North Ayrshire Council has advised that a change of use is required, but little progress has been recorded and the matter appears to be stuck; Cllr Murdoch reported in January 2026 that there had been no meetings. In February it was stated that the community group involved had not progressed the forms required. CCllr Woodburn agreed to email the Council for an update, and the action has been carried forward at every meeting since.
digest.responsible: North Ayrshire Council. LCC requesting updates.

digest.title: The future of St Columba's Church
digest.summary: A Friends of St Columba's group formed and was reported as active in January 2026. In February the Chair reported that, without warning, the church had been given a closing date for its sale the previous day. The Friends made a competitive offer, conditional on the Church of Scotland retaining the building while surveys were carried out and funding explored. The trustees were due to decide between bidders that evening. No later minutes record the outcome.
digest.responsible: Church of Scotland trustees. Friends of St Columba's.

digest.title: Off-licence application for Wetherspoons
digest.summary: An application by Wetherspoons to become an off-licence was considered. The Community Council agreed that it does not support the application, and the question of overprovision within the town was raised. The application was postponed to a hearing on 7 September 2026.

digest.title: North Ayrshire Council underspend and the school crossing patrols
digest.summary: North Ayrshire Council identified an underspend of £1.47 million and put three options for its use out for consideration. The Community Council proposed a fourth — using the money to protect the school crossing patrols and to acquire care capacity within the Health and Social Care Partnership — and agreed this unanimously. It was noted that a one-off underspend cannot fund continuing employment, though one-off grants could help various projects. The options return to full Council for a decision.
digest.responsible: North Ayrshire Council. LCC to write with its view.

digest.title: The seafront car park fund
digest.summary: Takings from the seafront car park rose by £100,000 after pay and display was installed. The Community Council recorded the view that residents should be able to suggest how the money is spent, with repairs to toilet facilities among the suggestions, and proposed discussing it with members of the public at a meeting. Councillors were due to meet on 22 June 2026 to consider the fund. In January the Council declined to approve money from the fund towards Christmas lights.

digest.title: Funding for the Christmas lights
digest.summary: Largs Events recorded difficulty securing a budget for the Christmas lights, and that North Ayrshire Council declined to approve money from the car park fund because of previous budget decisions. Council electricians were no longer certified to install on AMEY street furniture, and completing the installation through AMEY's appointed contractor cost Largs Events approximately £3,000. AMEY has put the cost forward to its community fund.
digest.responsible: Largs Events, with North Ayrshire Council and AMEY.

digest.title: Largs Colts and the Bowen Craig asset transfer
digest.summary: Kenny Armstrong, Chair of Largs Colts, set out the club's position following North Ayrshire Council's agreement to the community asset transfer of Bowen Craig. The club marked fifty years in 2025 and has around 100 volunteers giving time each week, 250 boys and girls playing football, and ten age groups from 5 to 17. Grass pitches can be used for about six months of the year, and other facilities in town cost approximately £25,000 to £30,000 a year; funds come from monthly subs, grant funding and fundraising. The stated aims for Bowen Craig are a financially sustainable year-round facility, raising the club's profile, engaging local providers and undertaking a sports facility needs assessment, consulting the community, and carrying out a site feasibility study.

digest.title: Electric vehicle charging hub at Hunterston
digest.summary: A proposal was presented for an electric vehicle charging hub at Hunterston, powered by renewable energy. It would work like a petrol forecourt but with charging points including ultra-rapid chargers, generating power on site by solar with additional supply from the national grid, and would include retail and coffee facilities. A planning application was expected within six to eight weeks.

digest.title: Power storage proposal at Hunterston
digest.summary: Highview Power notified LCC in November 2025 of proposals for a long duration energy storage facility at Hunterston PARC, with community events including a public event at West Kilbride Village Hall in January 2026. In February CCllr Macintosh reported back on the company's presentation of its proposals for power storage and a stability island at Hunterston, which indicated the development could possibly create around 1,000 jobs.

digest.title: Counterfeit notes in circulation
digest.summary: Reports were raised of counterfeit notes circulating locally, having been passed to businesses in the town. The notes feel slightly different, and the silver vertical hologram strip can be peeled away. It was agreed the problem should be communicated to residents to increase awareness. The Bank of England publishes guidance on checking notes.

digest.title: Review of the Scheme of Establishment
digest.summary: North Ayrshire Council is reviewing the Scheme of Establishment that governs community councils. LCC was encouraged in May 2025 to participate fully, with details of the process to be sent. In June it was reported that the whole scheme was open for review, with no proposal from North Ayrshire Council of what it wished to change, unlike other councils, and LCC agreed to seek the views of other community councils. A meeting to formulate a response was agreed in July. In September the consultation period was extended to allow further consultation. By May 2026 the review had still not been published and CCllr Woodburn agreed to email North Ayrshire Council for an update; in June it was recorded as likely later in the year. Community Council elections remain postponed until it concludes.

digest.title: One-hour parking in the town centre
digest.summary: A request was made in February 2025 to increase the one-hour parking limit in the town centre to two hours, with parents taking children to toddler groups finding one hour too limited. The blue badge procedure was also discussed. Cllr Marshall's recorded view was that one hour works well, because it is possible to park for longer elsewhere in town.

digest.title: Cycling Without Age trishaw rides
digest.summary: Cycling Without Age, which has around ninety branches in Scotland, presented to the April 2025 meeting. The Largs chapter has ten volunteer pilots and one trishaw, which anyone can ride, including children, for outings of roughly twenty minutes to an hour. Rides are booked by telephone. The chapter works with a local care home, taking residents out accompanied by a carer, and was raising funds towards a second trishaw at a cost of £10,000.

digest.title: Development at Hunterston PARC
digest.summary: The Hunterston PARC liaison committee reported to the April 2025 meeting. The site remained quiet, with remediation work under way and visits from Navy vessels, and a planning application was in process to begin work on tower foundations. XLCC was planning and modelling the site, a new construction company was being sought after the previous one ceased trading, and work was expected to begin in March 2026. Seventeen apprentices were training in Irvine with further places available. Filling the hole to allow construction of the marine yard, which would make turbine gravity bases, was estimated at £150 million, with Dutch companies bidding to supply suitable dredgings. A bond requires all above-ground structure to be removed if the business fails.

digest.title: The Viking Festival
digest.summary: The Viking Festival committee updated the May 2025 meeting on the festival's 45th year, with changes to the logo and to the programme of events. A longship was being built at the Maritime Museum in Irvine, with volunteers wanted for all aspects of the build, and the festival fire event was returning to Largs Thistle's football ground. A tug of war trophy was recovered for a competition, and a programme involving local businesses was to be free to the public; LCC agreed to take an advert in it, paid from the Admin account. Schools wanting to take part were invited to contact the committee. Coordinating with ScotRail was recorded as a challenge, with more buses possibly required. In June ScotRail advised that it could not provide extra trains during the festival because it clashes with the International Ayr Show, and the need for additional carriages, buses and ferries was raised. The programme had been printed with the support of local businesses, local traders would be at the event, and additional public toilets would be in place. LCC agreed to work directly with the festival directors and ScotRail on a plan for the following year.

digest.title: Planting in the town and the car park beds
digest.summary: Concern was raised in June 2025 about the neglect of planting in the town and the state of the flower beds at the car park. The Community Development Trust had started taking over some planters, and it was suggested that those at the car park may also need to be adopted.
digest.responsible: North Ayrshire Council. Some planters taken on by the Community Development Trust.

digest.title: Investment in Largs compared with the rest of North Ayrshire
digest.summary: Concern was raised in July 2025 about the amount of money spent in Largs compared with the rest of North Ayrshire, and Irvine in particular. It was recorded that every swimming pool in North Ayrshire other than the one in Largs, which is the oldest, has been replaced.

digest.title: A newsletter for the town
digest.summary: LCC recorded in August 2025 that it would like to produce a newsletter informing the public of events and activities in Largs, possibly working with the local paper and various groups, for the following summer. The new radio station at Largs Development Trust was also highlighted as a way of reaching people.

meeting.venueNote: Recent meetings have been held at Vikingar.
